verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 743 (XVII-35) shows three indentation levels in the ELEMENT column: statements at the margin (MOVE, MULTIPLY, OPEN); their elements one step in (TO identifier ... De-editing, BY identifier ... END-MULTIPLY, File-name ... EXTEND series); and WITH NO REWIND phrase / REVERSED phrase a further step in under INPUT phrase, and the second WITH NO REWIND phrase a further step in under OUTPUT phrase. The markdown page 743 has every element row flush, with no   or other marker, while page 742 of the same markdown encodes the same table's hierarchy with   (e.g. ' Data-name' under GENERATE statement). In this difference table the indentation is the only thing that says which element belongs to which statement or phrase, so its loss is content, not furniture: flush, WITH NO REWIND and REVERSED read as siblings of INPUT/OUTPUT phrase instead of sub-phrases of them. Row order and all level/module values are correct. The kind label 'misplaced-content' is loose; the defect is lost hierarchy (indentation) on every subordinate row of the page, not moved text.
